project.title: Farting Bin Engineering Challenge
project.challenge: Design, manufacture, program, test and evaluate an interactive school-bin insert that detects rubbish and plays a sound.

lessons.title: Project launch
lessons.student: Understand the challenge and examine the school bin.
lessons.evidence: Photo/notes: current bin and project problem.

lessons.title: Research mechanisms
lessons.student: Investigate switches, springs, impact plates and examples of interactive systems.

lessons.title: Success criteria
lessons.student: Create measurable criteria and constraints for a safe, reliable prototype.

lessons.title: Concept sketches
lessons.student: Develop at least two annotated design ideas and choose one.

lessons.title: Mechanical design
lessons.student: Plan plate size, spring positions, guide bolts and switch activation.

lessons.title: Laser-cut plates
lessons.student: Prepare or modify CAD files for top and bottom plates.

lessons.title: 3D switch holder
lessons.student: Model/check the microswitch holder against actual component dimensions.

lessons.title: Circuit and BOM
lessons.student: Complete circuit diagram and bill of materials.

lessons.title: Workshop safety
lessons.student: Complete laser/3D-print safety checks and prepare files.

lessons.title: Laser cut
lessons.student: Cut top and bottom plates; inspect accuracy.

lessons.title: 3D print
lessons.student: Print switch holder and test-fit the microswitch.

lessons.title: Mechanical assembly
lessons.student: Assemble springs, plates and switch mechanism.

lessons.title: Inputs and outputs
lessons.student: Identify input, processing and output components.

lessons.title: Arduino + switch
lessons.student: Wire the normally-open microswitch to Arduino D2 and GND.

lessons.title: DFPlayer + speaker
lessons.student: Wire and test the sound module and speaker.

lessons.title: Integrate electronics
lessons.student: Mount electronics safely away from rubbish.

lessons.title: Read switch input
lessons.student: Upload code that detects switch activation.

lessons.title: Play MP3
lessons.student: Trigger one sound reliably through DFPlayer.

lessons.title: Random sounds
lessons.student: Use randomisation to select different sound files.

lessons.title: Debounce and reset
lessons.student: Prevent repeated triggering and reset after the plate rises.

lessons.title: Create test plan
lessons.student: Design tests for different rubbish types and drop conditions.

lessons.title: Reliability testing
lessons.student: Complete at least 20 controlled drops and record results.

lessons.title: Improve prototype
lessons.student: Use evidence to change spring pressure, switch height, code or chute.

lessons.title: Retest
lessons.student: Repeat tests and compare performance.

lessons.title: Finalise prototype
lessons.student: Complete enclosure, wiring, labels and safety check.

lessons.title: Final evaluation
lessons.student: Evaluate the solution against every success criterion.

lessons.title: Demonstration
lessons.student: Demonstrate and explain the system to the class.

lessons.title: Reflection and submission
lessons.student: Complete individual reflection and submit final evidence.

rubric.a: Insightful problem definition; measurable criteria; multiple well-developed ideas; decisions strongly justified.
rubric.b: Clear problem definition and criteria; developed ideas; decisions justified.
rubric.c: Appropriate problem and criteria; workable design with some justification.
rubric.d: Basic problem/design information; limited justification or incomplete planning.
rubric.e: Minimal design evidence or solution is largely undocumented.

rubric.a: Accurate, robust manufacture; mechanism is well calibrated, reliable and refined.
rubric.b: Accurate manufacture; mechanism works reliably with minor issues.
rubric.c: Functional manufacture; mechanism works but has some inaccuracies or reliability issues.
rubric.d: Partially functional mechanism; significant construction or assembly issues.
rubric.e: Mechanical system incomplete or does not function.

rubric.a: Circuit is correct, safe, neat and fully integrated; excellent component protection and organisation.
rubric.b: Correct and safe circuit; well integrated with minor issues.
rubric.c: Circuit functions and is mostly safe; some wiring/integration issues.
rubric.d: Circuit partially functions or contains repeated wiring/integration problems.
rubric.e: Circuit is incomplete, unsafe or non-functional.

rubric.a: Well-structured, annotated code; robust input handling, random sound selection, debounce/reset and effective debugging.
rubric.b: Structured code with all major functions working; minor faults only.
rubric.c: Functional code that detects input and produces sound; some features or reliability are limited.
rubric.d: Partially functional code requiring substantial teacher assistance.
rubric.e: Code incomplete or does not operate the system.

rubric.a: Systematic testing; meaningful data; strong analysis; evidence-based improvements substantially increase performance.
rubric.b: Good testing and data; relevant improvements are justified and retested.
rubric.c: Appropriate testing; some data and improvement are evident.
rubric.d: Limited testing or improvement with little analysis.

rubric.a: Comprehensive individual evidence; precise evaluation against criteria; clear professional demonstration and reflection.
